propositions: Fourteen call sites hand-build identical single-turn structured request shapes with mode='structured', execution_mode='single_turn', output_schema, and four bounding seams, creating maintenance and silent-omission risk.
RunRequest's contract requires single_turn requests to carry mode='structured' and output_schema together, but this invariant is enforced only by hand-assertion at each site, not by the constructor.

Only one of fourteen sites (judge_batch) declares bounding seams; omission is indistinguishable from deliberate unbounding, allowing bugs like leathery-druidic-nurseshark (22da) where judge_one stayed unbounded for days.

A shared builder RunRequest.for_structured with required bounds argument and SingleTurnBounds dataclass will consolidate the repeated pattern, make bounding decisions explicit and greppable, and enforce the single-turn-structured invariant at construction.
The AST oracle test_subcall_class_selection.py must be taught to recognize RunRequest.for_structured(...) calls alongside direct RunRequest(...) calls to remain valid after adoption.

Adoption at all fourteen sites is byte-identical in resulting RunRequest objects; thirteen sites pass bounds=RunRequest.INHERIT_POLICY, judge_batch passes its existing four values, and completion_recovery.py passes token cap with other three None.
